output.brief: The remote promotion gap is mostly a matter of tenure, not location. Only 32% of remote staff have the 18 months in level that the policy requires, against 74% of office staff, because remote hiring only opened widely in July 2024. Among eligible people, nomination rates (28% vs 29%) and approval rates (71% vs 74%) are almost the same, and remote 20.0% vs office 21.1% eligible-to-approved. Applying office rates to the remote eligibility mix predicts 8.2%, against 7.6% observed. Remote attrition is not higher, and the gap shows in every job family, so neither job mix nor exits explain it. I'm fairly sure the gap is mainly an eligibility effect. The eligible remote group is only 110 people, so a real proximity effect of a few points can't be ruled out. The manager comments about handing urgent work to nearby staff are anecdotal and untested. Don't adopt the three-day office rule. It would penalise people hired on home-based contracts and rests on a misread comparison. Next: hold the proposal, report promotion rates for eligible people only, and check stretch-assignment allocation (staffing records) and the Committee's deferrals. Re-check at the FY2027 cycle. Briefings on the promotion criteria are reasonable but secondary.
